# System Design 101

> Learn system design from scratch: short Markdown pages, one idea each, backed by runnable code and primary sources.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): how the repo is organised and where to begin
- [Glossary](CONTEXT.md): one-line definitions of every term, linked to where it is taught
- [Page template](docs/_template.md): the fixed section order every page follows

## Foundations

- [How a request travels](docs/00-foundations/01-how-a-request-travels.md): from typing `google.com` to the server's front door: NAT, DNS, TCP, TLS, HTTP, gateway; how to read `dig`, `curl -v` and `traceroute` output

## Concepts

- [Communication styles](docs/concepts/communication/00-overview.md): request-response, server push or messaging, each with a real-world analogy; all 15 common terms (REST to Kafka) by group
- [API styles: GraphQL, gRPC, REST](docs/concepts/communication/01-api-styles.md): a real-world analogy for each, pros, cons, when to use each, design and run comparison tables, the same call in code, and a few lines each on JSON-RPC, SOAP and MCP
- [REST](docs/concepts/communication/02-rest.md): resources and URIs, methods (safe, idempotent), status codes, stateless requests, caching with ETag, OpenAPI, versioning, push with SSE, strict vs everyday REST (links in responses, pros and cons), and a FastAPI orders example
- [gRPC](docs/concepts/communication/03-grpc.md): RPC, the .proto contract, generated stub and servicer, four call types, HTTP/2 with the status in trailers, metadata, deadlines, retries, health and reflection, and a streaming example
- [Decision page template](docs/_template-decision.md): the fixed section order for pages that compare options

## Project

- [Foodpanda build log](project/foodpanda/README.md): each build step and the concepts it uses
- [auth_service](project/foodpanda/services/auth_service/README.md): FastAPI + JWT + Postgres authentication service

## Examples

- [Examples index](examples/README.md): every snippet with a one-line summary
- [Communication](examples/communication/): JSON vs Protobuf bytes for the same order
- [Concurrency](examples/concurrency/): mutex, RLock, semaphore, bounded semaphore, event, condition, barrier, GIL
- [Design patterns](examples/patterns/): singleton, factory method, abstract factory, builder, prototype
- [SOLID](examples/principles/solid/): the five principles, each with a bad and a good version

## Optional

- [Design spec](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-22-learning-hub-design.md): why the repo is shaped this way
